subject: Urgent: Medivance private cluster latency + 5xx surge
messages:
From: Dr. Amina Sayeed <amina@medivance.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Holt <james.holt@medivance.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2028 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden p95 spike and 502/503s on our private cluster

Laura —

We started seeing a large p95 latency jump on our private VPC deployment around 07:40 PST and a growing number of 502/503 responses on user-facing endpoints. The impact is visible in our logs and a handful of clinical workflows are timing out. We collected a short window of traces and attached two screenshots of the dashboard and the error waterfall (attached).

We need immediate help — can your team hop on this? Team here are seeing degraded throughput (QPS down ~40%) and some requests are getting routed to fallback variants with degraded quality. We are in the middle of a rollout but paused it when we saw the anomaly.

What we can share: a subset of request IDs, Vault-synced service account for access if you need it, and a short .tar of logs.

Thanks,
Amina
Dr. Amina Sayeed
VP Applied Clinical Informatics
Medivance Health

Attachments: screenshot_p95_20281130.png, svc-logs-medivance-20281130.tar.gz

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Amina Sayeed <amina@medivance.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2028 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike and 502/503s on our private cluster

Amina —

Thank you for the heads up and for sending the logs. We see the traces in the bundle and we’ve opened an internal incident. I’m elevating to our Private Deployments SREs and looping in Marissa and Jonas to lead the troubleshooting.

Immediate plan:
- Share run-level logs and the tarball to the incident Drive link (we’ll fetch via the service account)
- Snapshot the cluster config and current kernel/quantization profile
- Roll back the last canary if it looks correlated and if you’re comfortable
- If rollback isn’t viable, we’ll apply a targeted routing policy to steer traffic to the cold standby pool to keep your core workflows stable

Can you confirm whether the rollout included any quantization changes or custom kernel overrides? Also, please flag any SLA-priority routes (we’ll treat them first).

I’ll aim to have an initial triage update in 30 minutes.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2028 08:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike and 502/503s on our private cluster

Laura / team —

Quick notes from the SRE side after a first-pass on the logs:
- There is a correlated increase in time spent in kernel memcpy spins on the workers that are serving the hot shard (see trace IDs: t-7281, t-7284).
- Several workers hit a GC-like stall in the runtime when handling long-context requests; these were introduced by the canary that bumped max_context from 8k -> 20k.
- Error pattern for 502/503 points to a queue build-up at the ingress layer and downstream decode timeouts.

Immediate mitigations I recommend now:
1) Pause incoming canary traffic (we should reweight to previous stable flavor)
2) Apply a temporary per-route max_input_len cap for SLA routes to keep decode times bounded
3) Restart the 3 workers with the highest memcpy metrics (graceful restart) — I’ll coordinate with the ops agent in their VPC runbook

I’ll open INF-4823 and push the critical logs and a kernel-level flame chart to Drive. If kernel memcpy is the root cause we should consider a hotpatch that toggles an alternative memcpy kernel (we have a validated fallback compiled).

Marissa
Principal SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-runbook-medivance-20281130.pdf

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2028 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike and 502/503s on our private cluster

Acknowledging —

I’ve started the runtime metrics correlation and a quick smoke on the model variants. Early signal: the fallback variant has 25% higher decode time at long contexts which explains why routing to fallback increases tail latency under load.

Operational asks for exec/leadership sync (if we need to involve them):
- If Medivance requests capacity increase for the hot shard, we’ll need a temporary dedicated burst (estimate +3 GPUs) — finance needs sign-off for emergency credit if out of contract
- If rollback is rejected we should be prepared to throttle background batch jobs in Medivance’s deployment to free up CPU for decode paths

I’ll stand by for a quick call. We should prepare a 1-slide exec brief with impact (users affected, p95 delta, estimate to remediation) — Stephanie can you draft?

Jonas
Head of Private Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Amina Sayeed <amina@medivance.com>, James Holt <james.holt@medivance.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, ProcureOps <procureops@medivance.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2028 13:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike and 502/503s on our private cluster — update and next steps

Amina / James —

Update from our incident triage (summary):
- Root cause (under investigation): interaction between increased max_context in the canary and a memcpy kernel path that amplifies host-level copy time on large token windows. This produced ingress queue growth and decode timeouts for long-context routes.
- Impact: p95 increased from ~420ms -> ~1.1s for affected SLA routes; overall QPS reduced ~38% due to queue backpressure; 502/503s concentrated on two hot shards.

Actions we have executed now:
1) Paused canary and reweighted to last stable model variant (traffic rebalanced by 08:55 PST).
2) Gracefully restarted the three workers with highest memcpy metrics (expected recovery window 10–15 minutes per worker).
3) Applied temporary per-route input length cap for clinical SLA routes to keep decode bounded and preserve clinical throughput.
4) Collected kernel flame charts and uploaded all artifacts to the Drive link (see JIRA INF-4823).

Requested action from Medivance:
- Approve either a short rollback of the canary or approve a one-week capacity burst (+3 GPUs) while we validate the memcpy fallback kernel and run a staged rollout. Rolling back will restore baseline immediately, burst capacity will reduce tail pressure during revalidation.
- Provide permission for our ops agent to SSH into the three worker hosts for a targeted hotpatch if you choose the fallback kernel path. We have the patch validated in staging and it has a small perf delta for normal workloads.

If you prefer, we can set up a 20-minute exec huddle now with Jonas and our SREs to walk through impact and costs. Please reply with your preferred option (rollback vs burst + hotpatch) and whether ProcureOps should be looped for expedited credit.

Apologies for the disruption — we know clinical paths are high priority and we’ll keep this incident as the top ticket until resolved.

—Laura
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
